generated_by: Python reference implementation of the Focal speech experiments (2026-11-05) with the corrections of their audit and the rebuild decisions applied; the titles of sentences longer than TITLE_MAX follow the 2026-11-13 rule of Title.derive (whole words, the last clause that fills half of the room, no dangling function word, no ellipsis)
license_note: All sentences are synthetic and written for these tests; no corpus text.

conventions.token_times: start_s/dur_s as returned by sherpa-onnx (seconds, 80 ms grid); ms = floor(s*1000+0.5)
conventions.absolute_ms: word start/end = window.audio_start_ms + ms(token start) (+ ms(duration))
conventions.conf_min: min over content pieces of exp(logp), rounded to 6 decimals here; compare with tolerance 1e-6; null when a content piece has no logp
conventions.special_pieces: a <...> piece directly after a content piece lends its logp (min) to it and sets unknown_piece on its word; all are dropped before grouping
conventions.flagged_word_indices: not punct_only and (unknown_piece or conf_min < FLAG_THRESHOLD)
conventions.paragraphs: list of [first_word_index, end_index_exclusive] over the repaired word list
conventions.copy_text: paragraph words joined by ' ', paragraphs joined by '\n\n'
conventions.segments: runs of {quiet, energy, peak, ms}: 10 ms slots (quiet, peak) and 20 ms frames (energy)
conventions.windows: speech_ms = 10 * non-quiet slots owned by the window; peak = max slot peak owned; a slot is owned by the window containing its start, except that the slot straddling a break belongs to the window after it

segmenter_cases.description: Speech MIN+1 s, pause 0.6 s, speech 4 s: one pause cut PAUSE/2 into the pause; the next window starts 250 ms earlier (pure pause lead-in, no keep filter).
A pause that qualifies before MIN does not cut; the next one after MIN does.
A long pause that starts before MIN cuts as soon as the cut point reaches MIN.
Pauses shorter than PAUSE never cut; at MAX+OVERLAP/2 the hard cut goes to the centre of the longest quiet run in [start+MIN, start+MAX] (ties: earliest).
No quiet slots: hard cut at the lowest 5-frame energy sum in [start+MIN, start+MAX] (ties: earliest).
No quiet slots but an energy dip (VAD says speech, e.g. very quiet input): the hard cut lands in the dip.
Two qualifying pauses after MIN: cuts at both.
Long silence: one cut PAUSE/2 after the quiet run starts (MIN already reached).
Recording shorter than MIN: one FINAL window.

Recording ends 350 ms after the pause cut: audio_end of the pause window is clamped to total_ms (algorithms.md 1d lacks the clamp). decide_at_ms is also clamped to total_ms (Finish makes the window eligible immediately).

No quiet slot; frames 400-404 = [100,100,100,100,102] (sum 502), frames 500-504 = 100 each (sum 500): the later dip wins (cut 10050). Integer-dividing the sum by 5 gives a tie and would pick the earlier dip (8050).
A recording break (Pause/Resume) closes the open window at the break; the next window has no lead-in and no keep filter.
A break 450 ms after a pause cut: the pause window's right context and decide time stop at the break; the short window up to the break keeps its lead-in.
Silence continues: a new pause cut every MIN (the quiet run keeps counting); these windows have speech_ms 0 and a low peak.
The longest short pause has an odd length (70 ms): the hard cut lands on a 5 ms boundary; the slot straddling the cut belongs to the earlier window and the next search range uses floor indices.
A window whose own range is quiet but loud enough (peak above the silence floor): speech_ms 0, peak reported.
After a break the window restarts at the break: MIN/MAX are measured from it.

vad_hysteresis_cases.description: Speech is accepted only after p > 0.5 has lasted >= 1600 samples since the first window above threshold (the onset window itself returns false).
Once speaking, p between 0.35 and 0.5 keeps speech.
While speaking, p <= 0.35 (the negative threshold) starts the silence timer; speech ends once it has run >= 800 samples. Only p > 0.5 resets it.
A single window above threshold is not speech.
tempEnd is reset only by p > threshold, not by 0.35 < p < 0.5: the second p=0.1 window ends speech immediately (an implementation that resets the timer on p > 0.35 returns true there).
p == threshold is neither > nor <: while triggered it still counts as speech (p > neg_threshold); before triggering it changes nothing (tempStart is not cleared).
